children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares gave up early gains to trade little changed on Wednesday as investors turned risk-averse ahead of a long holiday break.
** The benchmark KOSPI
was up 11.26 points, or 0.16%, at 7,029.17, as of 0214 GMT, after rising nearly 2% earlier in the session.
** The Nasdaq
notched a record-high close on Tuesday, lifted by Micron Technology
and other AI-related stocks, while the S&P 500
hovered just below a record high as oil prices traded around $100 per barrel.
** South Korean financial markets will be closed on Thursday and Friday for Chuseok holidays.

** South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and US President Donald Trump welcomed "significant progress" in discussions on strategic investment projects during a 30-minute meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Seoul's presidential office said.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
was up 1.90% and SK Hynix
was higher 0.11%, after rising sharply earlier in the session on an overnight rally in US peers.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
climbed 0.29%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were down 1.94% and 1.86%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 1.89%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
fell 0.93%.
** Of the total 910 traded issues, 292 shares advanced, while 566 declined.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 188.1 billion won ($139.14 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,351.0 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.41% higher than its previous close at 1,356.5.
** In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.08 point to 102.37.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 0.8 basis point to 4.016%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 5.5 basis points to 4.409%.
